# AI Assistant — Vars

Var definitions are derived from `module.lowdefy.yaml`. Pass these via the `vars:` block in your app's `lowdefy.yaml` entry for this module.

## Summary

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | string |  | Yes | Id of the app agent the chat talks to (an entry under the app's `agents`). The module does not define an agent — the system prompt, model, and tools are the app's business. |
| `scope` |  |  | Yes | Runtime operator resolving to the string that partitions threads, e.g. `{_state: record_id}`. Threads are listed and created against (scope, session user), so the same page in a different scope is a different set of threads. Use a constant string for a single global assistant. Resolved each time it is used — minting, listing, saving — so a value that arrives late is not frozen as null. A scope that CHANGES mid-session needs the consumer to clear the open thread on visit; the module cannot observe an app global moving. See "Scope" in the module docs. |
| `page_id` | string | `ai-assistant` |  | Stamped on saved threads so they can be traced back to a surface. |
| `visible` |  | `true` |  | Runtime operator gating the whole panel INCLUDING its launcher — e.g. `{_state: loaded}`, so the assistant appears with the page's content rather than over its skeleton. Read only by the `panel` component; the `embedded` component's visibility is its page's business. |
| `panel_title` |  | `Assistant` |  | Panel header title. Takes the app display font when one is defined. |
| `panel_subtitle` |  |  |  | Small line under the title — an identity or status line, not a sentence. |
| `panel_avatar_icon` |  | `AiOutlineRobot` |  | Icon in the round mark left of the title. |
| `panel_launcher_icon` |  | `AiOutlineRobot` |  | Icon on the closed launcher. |
| `panel_launcher_label` |  |  |  | Optional text pill beside the launcher while closed. Leave null for a circular icon-only launcher. |
| `panel_launcher_aria_label` |  | `Open assistant` |  | Accessible name for the launcher. Always meaningful, label or not. |
| `panel_width` |  | `420` |  | Panel width in px. ~420 is about 62 characters of chat. |
| `panel_expanded_width` |  | `760` |  | Panel width in px when expanded with the header control. |
| `panel_height` |  | `660` |  | Panel height in px. Always clamped to the viewport. |
| `panel_placement` |  | `bottom-right` |  | Corner the launcher and panel anchor to — bottom-right or bottom-left. |
| `embedded_height` | string | `65vh` |  | CSS height of the `embedded` component's chat area (and its thread list, which swaps in over the same space). Any CSS length; the default keeps a composer on screen for most viewports. |
| `shared_state` | object | `{}` |  | Object of runtime operators handed to the agent with every message, so the assistant knows what the user is looking at right now. This is the module's main seam: everything domain-specific about the conversation enters here. |
| `welcome` | object | `{}` |  | The empty-thread screen — { title, description, prompts }, where prompts is a list of { label, description } suggestion cards. |
| `sender_placeholder` | string | `Ask a question…` |  |  |
| `thinking_messages` | array | `[]` |  | Rotating status lines shown while the agent works. App-specific on purpose: generic ones ("Thinking…") waste the one moment the user is watching. |
| `message_display` | object | `{}` |  | Overrides merged over the module's AgentChat messageDisplay defaults (assistant name, reasoning/tool display, copy action). |
| `on_before_send` | array | `[]` |  | Actions run before a message is sent, on the chat block's onBeforeSend. Throw here to refuse the send — this is where a per-user quota or an entitlement check belongs, since it is the only seam that runs before the model is called. |
| `on_user_message` | array | `[]` |  | Actions run when the user sends a message, on the chat block's onUserMessage. For the app's own record of what was asked; the module already persists the message itself. |
| `on_data_part` | array | `[]` |  | Actions run for each custom data part the agent streams, on the chat block's onDataPart. Filter on the part type: the module does not, so every part reaches these actions. |
| `feedback_values` | object | `{}` |  | Ratings already stored for the OPEN thread, keyed by message id, each `like` or `dislike` — the block's own vocabulary, as `on_feedback` reports it. The chat block persists no rating, so without this a reload or a thread switch shows every message unrated even where the app recorded it, which reads as a lost write rather than a display gap. Storing remains the app's job; this only hands back what it stored. A rating clicked during the visit takes precedence, so the thumb still responds immediately. Rebuild it for the thread being opened — `on_thread_change` is the seam for that. |
| `on_feedback` | array | `[]` |  | Actions run when the user rates a message, on the chat block's onFeedback. Only reachable when the feedback action is enabled through `message_display`; leaving this empty while enabling that control renders a button that does nothing. |
| `on_thread_change` | array | `[]` |  | Actions run whenever the ACTIVE thread changes by a user action — opening one from the thread list, or starting a new chat. Not run by `enter`: a page splices its own actions after `enter` directly, and firing both would run them twice on the first visit. For anything the consumer derives from the open conversation and renders outside the chat — a references panel, filters keyed to the current answer. Without it such state is built once on mount and then silently belongs to the wrong thread the moment the user switches, which reads as stale data rather than as missing data. Read the new thread from `_state: ai_conversation_id`, which is committed before these actions run. Not from the event: the two call sites deliver different ones (a thread-list click, a new-chat button press), and only the state is common. |
| `on_link_click` |  |  |  | Actions run when the user clicks a link inside a message, on the chat block's onLinkClick. The event carries `href` and `text`. Use it to open an in-app target in place instead of navigating out of the conversation. Leaving this empty changes nothing: the anchor's own navigation is suppressed only when actions are supplied. Once wired, interception covers the whole message — an href you do not recognise navigates nowhere, so handle the fall-through. Modified and non-primary clicks are never delivered, so open-in-new-tab keeps working. Takes either a plain action array or the full `{ try, catch }` event form. |
| `tag` |  |  |  | Runtime operator resolving to a short LABEL to attach to the thread on each save, accumulated as a set and shown as chips on the thread cards — e.g. the title of the record being discussed. Stored as the display string, not an id: the module cannot resolve app ids, and a thread list is a historical record of what was discussed. Null to disable chips. |
| `generate_titles` | boolean | `true` |  | Name each thread from its FIRST EXCHANGE — the opening question and the reply together — once the first reply lands. Prefer this to an agent's own generateTitle, which sees only the opening message; where that message is a canned suggestion prompt, every thread ends up with the same name. Turn off to keep the provisional title (the user's first message, truncated) and skip the model call — the AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY secret is only used when this is on. |
| `title_context` |  |  |  | Runtime operator resolving to one line of grounding for the title generator, e.g. "Acme Ltd — onboarding". Lets it name the subject when the exchange only ever says "this record". |
| `title_domain` | string |  |  | One phrase describing the app for the title generator's vocabulary, e.g. "a staffing and payroll tool". Null for a generic prompt. |
| `title_model` | string | `openai/gpt-5-mini` |  | Gateway model id for the titling call. Small and fast is the right choice. |
| `collection` | string | `conversations` |  | MongoDB collection holding threads. |
